The *Paccuggamaniyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 285) is a biographical poem preserved within the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts the past-life deeds and spiritual aspirations of the elder Paccuggamaniya. On SuttaCentral, five modern translations of the text across five languages are registered [SuttaCentral].

No external parallels in Chinese, Tibetan, or Sanskrit have been identified for this text [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal formulaic reuse across verse collections and commentaries [DharmaNexus]. The text shares passages heavily with the commentary to the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, both parts, accounting for 19 shared matches), as well as with other poems in the *Therāpadāna*, such as *Akkantasaññakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 220), *Sovaṇṇavaṭaṁsakiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 229), *Nimittasaññakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 327), *Yūthikapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 202), and *Paccāgamaniyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 65) [DharmaNexus].
